signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitics + Carry + Vol
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 163.67, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following headlines that a U.S.–Iran deal is within reach. This shift in risk appetite triggers a sharp 5.02% sell-off in WTI oil and a retreat in gold, removing the immediate safe-haven floor for the Yen. A 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage (3.75% vs 1.0%) remains the structural anchor, while JPY COT LF net shorts at -114,030 show speculators remain heavily positioned for further weakness. The 25d Risk Reversal at -1.49 indicates the options market is still paying a premium for downside protection despite the spot bid, likely reflecting BoJ meeting risk on July 31. USD/JPY vs US 10Y correlation has broken to +0.475 (z=+1.65σ), suggesting the pair is now driven more by headline risk-on flows than traditional yield spreads. Risk: BoJ delivers a hawkish surprise on July 31, triggering a disorderly unwind of the crowded spec short.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Positioning + ESI + CB Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5799, supported by a strong positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +22.2, contrasting with the negative EUR ESI of -9.5. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. While the nominal carry favors the USD by 125bp, the real policy rate differential is narrower, with NZD real rates at -1.56% vs USD at +1.47%. Price has cleared the SMA20 at 0.5765, signaling a shift in intraday momentum that challenges the crowded institutional short. The RBNZ hike bias provides a fundamental floor that speculators are currently ignoring at their peril. Risk: RBNZ pivots to a hold stance at the September 2 meeting, validating the existing spec short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing the 0.6988 level, supported by a 60bp carry advantage for the AUD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%) and a hawkish stance from Governor Bullock. Volatility pricing is extreme, with AUD/USD IV at 14.7% vs HV30 of 6.0%, resulting in a massive +8.7% Vol Risk Premium (VRP). Retail sentiment is 65% short, diverging from the COT LF net long position of +20,521, which historically favors further upside as retail fades the institutional trend. Technicals show the pair holding above its SMA20 (0.6962) and SMA200 (0.6904), though the SMA50 at 0.7024 acts as immediate resistance. High VRP suggests the market is pricing in a significant move around upcoming RBA and Fed volatility. Risk: RBA shifts to a neutral bias at the August 11 meeting, eroding the AUD carry premium.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility + Technicals
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1405, remaining stuck in a bearish technical posture below its SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200 cluster (1.1417–1.1637). Options markets show an elevated Vol Risk Premium (VRP) of +2.5%, with IV at 7.1% vs HV30 at 4.6%, indicating that traders are paying up for protection ahead of the September 10 ECB meeting. Despite the ECB's hiking bias, the 135bp nominal carry disadvantage against the USD (ECB 2.4% vs Fed 3.75%) limits upside potential. COT LF net shorts at -80,570 align with the negative ESI of -9.5, confirming that both data and positioning are weighted against the Euro. A sustained break above the SMA20 at 1.1417 is required to neutralize the immediate bearish outlook. Risk: ECB signals a pause in September, further widening the policy divergence with the Fed.
